items.title: Deputy Mayor Wilton called the meeting to order.
Deputy Mayor Wilton read the land acknowledgement.
Addendums and Corrections to the Agenda
There were no addendums or corrections to the agenda.
Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest Under the Municipal Conflict of Interest
John Scott, Greenlanes indicated his preference for the multi-use pad
notes: proposed for Bissell Park to be open, welcoming, inclusive and without boards. He expressed concerns with a design that only promotes hockey and encouraged an open skating rink similar to Nathan Phillips Square in Toronto or the skating rink/splash pad in front of City Hall in Guelph. He wished to see a continuation of all the existing uses in the space and responded to questions.

items.title: Bissell Park Multi-use Pad Project Update
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services provided an overview of the report, including details of the current condition of the existing facility, project background and current status, a summary of the request, and the proposed project time frame.

Tom Keating, Elora Rockers / Keating Construction introduced David Alves as a dedicated member of the community with 41 years of volunteer service with the ice surface at Bissel Park. He explained the reasons for the delay, the challenges with the project, the financial commitment to date and the desire to see the Township take the lead on over seeing the completion of the project. He indicated an ongoing commitment of support for the project by both the Elora Rockers and the Elora Lions Club and noted thei support includes future fund-raising efforts.

Staff and T. Keating responded to questions regarding the role of the Elora Rockers and Lions Club in conjunction with the Healthy Communities Advisory Committee, the ongoing community support and fund-raising efforts, the safety of the existing pad, and the necessary geotechnical work to be undertaken.

items.title: Code of Conduct for Council Members & Members of Local Boards
notes: Report from K. O'Kane, Manager of Legislative Services and Municipal Clerk
John Mascarin, Aird & Berlis LLP, presented the draft Code of Conduct for Council Members & Members of Local Boards and provided an overview of the role of the Integrity Commissioner.

J. Mascarin responded to questions regarding the advice-giving and reporting function of the Integrity Commissioner, recommendations of penalties and/or remedial measures or corrective actions and investigative obligations.

motions.text: THAT the minutes of the Public Meetings under the Planning Act held April 26, and July 26, 2023 be adopted as circulated.
motions.text_html: THAT the minutes of the Public Meetings under the Planning Act held April 26, and July 26, 2023 be adopted as circulated.

motions.item_title: Bissell Park Multi-use Pad Project Update
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington terminate the Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad Project: Jack R MacDonald Grant Agreement, dated September 1, 2020 between the Township of Centre Wellington, James Keating Construction Ltd., and the Elora Lions Club; AND THAT Council approves the allocation of $413,255.52 in existing funds to the Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad Project as outlined in report CS2023-21 dated August 14, 2023; AND THAT Council directs staff to issue a Request for Proposal to hire a consultant for conceptual and detailed design, construction ready documents, and a Class A construction budget, to an upset limit of $100,000; AND THAT Council establish a Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad Project Working Group (under the Healthy Communities Advisory Committee) which will include members of the advisory committee as well as representatives from the Elora Rockers and the Elora Lions Club.
